x: Kerala has India's highest road density (6,690.30 km per 1,000 sq km on 31 March 2019; 517.77 per 100 sq km in NCERT's 2011 data), far above Punjab (2,935.98), Gujarat and Haryana.

x: PMGSY (25 December 2000) is a rural roads scheme giving all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations, so the road-connectivity option is the answer; patrolling, crime response and 'community life' are not its aim. x: The East-West Corridor runs from Silchar (Assam) to Porbandar (Gujarat) and meets the North-South Corridor at Jhansi; it is not Dibrugarh-Surat or any of the other pairs.
source: NextGen Indian Geography - APPSC Exams Part 8.1 p.3 (book p.143); OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.15 (book p.92)

x: Leningrad (St. Petersburg), Moscow and Vladivostok are all on the Trans-Siberian route; Georgia is a separate country in the Caucasus, not a station.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.19 (book p.95); PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 2 p.7-10 (book pp.120-122)

x: The Trans-Siberian main line runs from Moscow to Vladivostok (9,289 km, 8 time zones). NCERT and PMF trace the route from St. Petersburg, but the railway itself is the Moscow-Vladivostok line; Khabarovsk is only an intermediate city.
source: NextGen Rocket World Geography #17 p.27-28 ('Moscow → Vladivostok'); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-Siberian_Railway (termini Moscow Yaroslavsky – Vladivostok, 9,289 km)
evidence: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.19 (book p.95) (St. Petersburg – Vladivostok, 9,332 km)
PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 2 p.7-10 (book pp.120-122)

x: The Channel Tunnel (Eurotunnel) runs under the English Channel and links England (UK) with France (London-Paris); Holland, Belgium and Luxembourg are not its ends.
source: NextGen Rocket World Geography #17 p.27-28 (p.28); PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 2 p.7 (book p.120)

x: The Canadian Pacific, Canada's first transcontinental line (1885), runs from Montreal to Vancouver. Halifax-Vancouver is how NCERT describes the 'Trans-Canadian' line, so it is the tempting wrong option for the CPR.
source: NextGen Rocket World Geography #17 p.27-28 ('Canadian Pacific Railway – Montreal / Vancouver')
evidence: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.19 (Trans-Canadian: Halifax – Vancouver)
PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 2 p.8 (book p.121)

x: The Trans-Canada Highway links Vancouver (British Columbia, west coast) with St. John's in Newfoundland (east coast), which the option calls 'Saint John City'. Montreal, Toronto and Quebec are only on the way.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.14 (book p.91); PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 2 p.5 (book p.118)

x: The Trans-Siberian (Moscow-Vladivostok, 9,289 km) is the longest continuous railway in the world; the Canadian National and Canadian Pacific lines are much shorter, and there is no 'Transatlantic Railway'.
source: NextGen Rocket World Geography #17 p.27-28; OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.19 (book p.95)

x: The Orient Express (Paris-Istanbul) ran across France, Germany, Austria, Hungary and Romania; the Trans-Siberian is in Russia, the Cape-Cairo line in Africa and the Union/Central Pacific in the USA.
source: PMF Human & Economic Geography Part 2 p.7-10 (book pp.120-122) (p.10: via Strasbourg, Munich, Vienna, Budapest); NextGen Rocket World Geography #17 p.27-28

x: Trans-Andean = Buenos Aires-Valparaiso (4), Trans-Siberian = Leningrad-Vladivostok (2), Orient Express = Paris-Istanbul (1), leaving the European Trans-Continental = Paris-Warsaw (5): code 5 4 2 1.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.16, p.19 (book pp.93-95); NextGen Rocket World Geography #17 p.27-28

x: Sochi is a Black Sea resort in south-west Russia, far from the Trans-Siberian; Kazan (on a connecting branch), Omsk and Chita are on the route.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT Human Geography Part 8 p.19 (book p.95) (Chita on the route); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trans-Siberian_Railway (route map: Omsk, Chita; line 'from Kazan')
